history.summary: POSSIBLE CSV DUPLICATE FLAG: a sibling task is researching CSV row 902 'Sai Mandir' Namchi - the documented shrine below appears to be the same Sai Mandir of Namchi (at Assangthang), so rows 902 and 905 may be duplicates of each other; confirm before listing twice. This is the well-documented Sai Mandir, a Hindu pilgrimage centre dedicated to Shirdi Sai Baba, situated in the Assangthang area of Namchi, South Sikkim, about 3 km from the Solophok Char Dham. It was built in 2010 by the Government of Sikkim and opened on 3 November 2010 as a gift of Chief Minister Dr. Pawan Kumar Chamling to the people of Sikkim. The two-storey temple has a golden facade with gold accents; the idol of Sai Baba (white marble, in the style of the Shirdi original) is placed on the first floor per one travel guide, while another guide describes the main prayer hall on the ground floor with the idol at its centre (CONFLICT between sources - verify floor layout). The hall also carries ten paintings of the Dashavataras of Vishnu. A garden around the temple offers panoramic views of Mt. Kanchenjunga. Zee Zest places the Sai Mandir in the centre of Namchi town rather than Assangthang (CONFLICT - verify; Assangthang is the better-attested location). Note: a different Sai Baba temple is also listed at Mangan, North Sikkim (approx. 27.5 miles from Namchi per a location database) - not this shrine (verify).

name: Shirdi Sai Baba Mandir, Namchi
town_description: Namchi, headquarters of Namchi (South Sikkim) district at about 1,315 m, is a major pilgrimage and tourism centre of Sikkim. Around it lie the Char Dham (Solophok), the Samdruptse Guru Padmasambhava statue, the Sai Mandir at Assangthang, Ngadak and Ralang monasteries, and the Temi Tea Garden - Sikkim's only tea garden.

travel.airport: Nearest airport is Bagdogra (IXB), West Bengal, approx. 90-100 km from Namchi (verify); Pakyong Airport is closer but has limited flights.
travel.railway: Nearest major railway station is New Jalpaiguri (NJP), approx. 90-100 km; Siliguri is the road hub.
travel.road: About 3 km from the Solophok Char Dham near Namchi; reachable by local taxi or shared jeep from Namchi town (verify exact distance and route).

visitor_information.best_time: October to March for pleasant weather and clear mountain views; Guru Poornima brings special observances (verify).
visitor_information.opening_hours: Listed as 6:00 AM to 6:00 PM (verify); no entry fee, donations accepted for maintenance (verify). Note: the geocoded location point for the Sai Baba temple in Namchi (Apatan Marg, 27.1667, 88.3650) may refer to a smaller in-town shrine rather than the Assangthang temple - treat coordinates as approximate for Namchi.
